html:
The Carolingian Empire was the Frankish empire of Charlemagne and his heirs, covering most of western and central Europe from 800 to 888. It is on the map for 800 and 900.

It grew from the Frankish kingdoms. Charlemagne conquered the Lombards of Italy in 774, the Saxons after some thirty years of war, and the Avars on the Danube. On Christmas Day 800 Pope Leo III crowned him emperor in Rome. He ruled through counts and travelling inspectors, and from his court at Aachen he backed a revival of learning and a clear new handwriting.

His son Louis the Pious held it together with difficulty. His grandsons split it by the Treaty of Verdun in 843 into West Francia, a middle kingdom, and East Francia, the ancestors of France and Germany. It was briefly reunited under Charles the Fat and finally broke up in 888. The idea of a western emperor lived on in the Holy Roman Empire.
sum: The Carolingian Empire was the Frankish empire of Charlemagne and his heirs, covering most of western and central Europe from 800 to 888. It is on the map for 800 and 900.
